note: The CI toolchain every eligible host must hold, tracked in git. The host list is host-local and never committed: ~/.local/lib/marscode/ci-hosts.json (or SHIP_QUEUE_CI_HOSTS) holds only `hosts`, and the loader takes `toolchain` and `guards` from this file. `ship-queue hosts check` prints each host's drift against it; `ship-queue hosts provision [HOST]` installs what a host lacks. Add a tool here, never on one host: a tool that a CI step or toolchainEnv.ts needs must have an entry, and each pinned version has a pin in sq_pins.json.

biome.note: a JS and CSS linter a repo may declare as its own lint step (a repo declares it, ship_ci_tool=biome); in ship-queue-ci/npm/bin, on every CI step's PATH. The playbook runs no Biome of its own

gh.note: the playbook's gates ask GitHub whether each issue a Baseline entry or an approval marker cites is open; gh reads its own login

go.note: a Go toolchain, user-level or a system package: a repo declares go vet, go build and golang.org/x/tools deadcode (fetched by go run into the data root's module cache) as its Go lint, typecheck and deadcode steps, and a repo's suites build with it

docker.note: required by any repo that declares ship_ci_service; the engine's version, so an engine that does not answer is drift and routing keeps service jobs off the host; the install restarts an engine the user owns (OrbStack, Docker Desktop, rootless) and says when only an admin can (a system dockerd, no docker)

node.note: the floor is the release every CI host runs, so a host with an older node is drift; ci-node.sh reads the release from this range and installs it, checked against the sha256 per platform given here (the release's SHASUMS256.txt; Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64 and macOS arm64), into ship-queue-ci/node-v<version>-<platform>, and the guards step moves the host guards' node shim to it when the node the shim runs is older

pnpm.install: t="$HOME/.local/share/ship-queue-ci"; [ "$("$t/npm/bin/pnpm" --version 2>/dev/null)" = 9.15.9 ] || npm install -g --prefix "$t/npm" pnpm@9.15.9; if [ -d "$t/npm/lib/node_modules/corepack" ]; then npm uninstall -g --prefix "$t/npm" corepack; fi; rm -rf "$t/corepack"; for b in pnpm pnpx corepack; do l="$HOME/.local/bin/$b"; if [ -L "$l" ]; then case "$(readlink "$l")" in "$t/"*) rm -f "$l" ;; esac; fi; done

playbook.note: MarsCode's own: every provision reinstalls it from the queue's source checkout

fly.note: the live fleet check lists the Fly account with it; provision installs the fleet-check CLIs on every CI host and hosts check reports one without them; a repo whose CI lists the accounts declares them (ship_ci_tool), so routing never sends its job to a host that lacks one. google-chrome.note: Google Chrome, which a repo's browser gate runs in (Playwright's channel "chrome", for its codecs): the CURRENT stable release, never a pinned one (a pinned browser stays on a release with known security defects). Every provision runs ci-chrome.sh (refresh), so a host moves to the newer stable at its next provision; the range is only a floor (157, the stable when the tool was added), with no upper bound. What is fixed is who signs: signed-by= is the fingerprint of Google's Linux package signing key, and ci-chrome.sh installs only what Google's apt repository names under a good signature of that key (the Release file's signature, then the package list's sha256 from it, then the package's sha256 from the list), all over HTTPS from dl.google.com. No root: the package is unpacked (never installed as a package) into <data root>/ship-queue-ci/google-chrome-<version>; ~/.local/share/ship-queue-ci/google-chrome links to its opt/google/chrome, the stable place of the chrome executable a repo's Playwright config names as executablePath (channel "chrome" looks only in /opt/google/chrome), and google-chrome is a command in ship-queue-ci/bin, on every CI step's PATH. A host that also has Chrome as a system package (the queue host: its desktop user's own browser) gets the user-level copy too, so the CI's browser is the same on every host; the system package is not changed or shadowed, because google-chrome is in ship-queue-ci/bin, which only the CI steps' PATH has, before /usr/bin there. That command refuses to start without --user-data-dir, so a CI step never opens the desktop user's profile. Chrome's setuid sandbox needs root and is not installed: Playwright starts Chrome with no sandbox by default. Linux only: the gates that need Chrome run on Linux

hardware-gpu.note: a hardware GPU as a browser gets it: a capability only some Linux hosts have, so a job that declares it goes only to a host where the google-chrome on PATH, headless, gets a real GPU for WebGL by the host's own GPU path. The path depends on the host, not on the repo: a native Linux host has a Vulkan driver (--use-angle=vulkan and the rest); WSL has none, and reaches its GPU through Mesa's d3d12 driver (--use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl-egl, with GALLIUM_DRIVER=d3d12 in the browser's environment). The probe (ci-chrome.sh gpu) answers from a record that says hardware=1, measured within 6 h with the same Chrome build, and starts no browser; else it measures, the path that last worked (or d3d12 on WSL) first with most of a 25 s budget, and a run where every path ran out of time leaves a record of hardware=1 for this build standing up to 24 h (`ci-chrome.sh measure-gpu` always measures). Measuring, it tries the paths in that order, records the first that gives a real GPU of its own kind in ~/.local/share/ship-queue-ci/chrome-gpu, and while that record says hardware every CI step on that host gets it as SHIP_QUEUE_CHROME_GPU_ARGS and SHIP_QUEUE_CHROME_GPU_ENV, so the probe measures what a gate then gets. It measures the browser, not the kernel's device list. Never provisioned, and a host without it is not drift; the probe prints a constant (it has no version)

hcloud.note: the live fleet check lists the Hetzner servers with it

op.note: the live fleet check lists the 1Password vaults, and a repo's checks read its read-only fleet tokens, with it

doppler.note: the live fleet check lists the Doppler configs, and a repo's live config checks read them, with it

xz.note: xz, which tar runs to unpack the pinned .tar.xz builds (node, shellcheck, ffmpeg): a bare Ubuntu machine has none

gpg.note: gpg, which ci-chrome.sh checks the signature of Google's package list with: a bare Ubuntu machine has none

docker-compose.note: the compose plugin of docker (docker compose ...); on a bare Linux host the queue asks root for Ubuntu's docker-compose-v2, without its Recommends (docker.io: a second dockerd beside docker-ce; the Mac's guest had it installed by hand)

The probe runs no install: it prints the version only when each build the dry run names has Playwright's INSTALLATION_COMPLETE and DEPENDENCIES_VALIDATED markers (the host check passed; an admin installs what it lacks, `npx playwright-core@<version> install-deps webkit` as root: libavif16 on Ubuntu 24.04 with WebKitGTK, GTK 4 and GStreamer on a bare one) and dbus-run-session is there on Linux (the check runs WebKit in a private session)

webkit-video.note: headless WebKit presents decoded H.264 frames: a repo's browser gate plays video in Playwright's WebKit and reads the frames WebKit presented. The probe (ci-webkit-video.sh probe) plays a short H.264 clip in the CI's own playwright-core WebKit and passes when it presents frames. It needs the GStreamer GL plugin, gstreamer1.0-gl, an admin's system package (the root grant; Playwright's install-deps webkit does not install it): without it WebKit takes a software video path that holds a video paused after a few frames. It tries the host's own decoder selection first, then the NVIDIA (CUDA) decoders out of the selection, for WSL, where CUDA cannot share frames with GL; it records the first that presents frames in ~/.local/share/ship-queue-ci/webkit-video, and while that record says presents=1 every CI step on that host gets its GST_PLUGIN_FEATURE_RANK word (ship-queue-hygiene.sh). Every Linux host must pass: a host whose WebKit presents no frame is drift. The probe prints a constant (it has no version)

docker-shared-root.note: a container the CI's Docker starts can bind the host's / with rslave propagation (a node-exporter does): the probe starts one, on a pinned busybox it pulls once, so the daemon itself judges the mount. An admin step where it fails: make / a shared mount (on WSL 2: /etc/wsl.conf [boot] command = mount --make-rshared /, then wsl --shutdown)

docker-watchdog.note: a launchd agent that runs ci-docker-engine.sh watch every 10 minutes and at load: it restarts a Docker engine that stops answering (OrbStack hangs while a Mac sleeps unused) and once a day removes build cache older than 7 days and dangling images, never a container or a volume; its log is ~/.local/share/ship-queue-ci/docker-watchdog/watch.log; the probe passes only while the agent runs the provisioned copy of the script, and every provision runs the install (refresh), which leaves an agent already running the current script and plist alone; the version is the agent's (WATCHDOG_VERSION), raised when the agent itself changes

gnu-userland.note: GNU coreutils, sed, findutils and grep, and a setsid, first on a macOS CI step's PATH (CI_PATH_SETUP, scripts/ship/ci-runner.py): the CI runs the same stat -c, sed -i, date -d, touch -d, realpath -m, paste and timeout on every host; pinned GNU releases built from source, each tarball checked against the sha256 in ci-gnu-userland.sh; the version is the bundle's (gnu/BUNDLE), raised when a pin or a program changes (5: setsid and flock with util-linux's options, no tar; 6: flock refuses a bad number as util-linux does); Linux hosts have the GNU userland natively

linux.note: the Linux kernel itself, for a CI setting whose suites are built on it (for example inotify, netlink sock_diag and /proc, or an emulator with KVM): every Linux host has it, no Mac does, so routing sends such a job to a Linux host; nothing to install

cc.note: a C compiler: cargo links with it, and a Mac's GNU bundle builds its setsid and flock with it (ci-gnu-userland.sh; ci-gnu-userland.test.sh builds them on every host); an admin installs build-essential (Linux) or Xcode's command line tools (macOS)

jdk.note: a JDK for the Kotlin and Android tools (ktlint): Eclipse Temurin 17.0.21+9, the October 2026 critical patch update; ci-jvm.sh installs the vendor's tarball for Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64 or macOS arm64, checked against the release's own sha256 (its .sha256.txt), into <data root>/ship-queue-ci/jdk-<release>; ~/.local/share/ship-queue-ci/jdk links to its home, and java and javac are links in ship-queue-ci/bin, on every CI step's PATH; no system package and no JAVA_HOME (the java on PATH finds its own home)

ktlint.note: the Kotlin linter: the release's one self-running jar for every platform, which runs the java on PATH (the jdk tool, installed before it); checked against the sha256 GitHub records for the release asset (the release is also PGP-signed by the ktlint signing key, ADBC987D1A7B91DB6B0AAA81995EFBF4A3D20BEB), into <data root>/ship-queue-ci/ktlint-<version>, linked from ship-queue-ci/bin; it embeds Kotlin 2.2.21: CVE-2026-53914 (Kotlin < 2.4.20) is in the build cache metadata, which ktlint never reads (it parses source), and no ktlint release embeds 2.4.20 yet

webkit2gtk-4.1.note: WebKitGTK 4.1's development files, which a Tauri app's cargo check builds against: a capability only some Linux hosts have (an admin's system package, libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev), so a job that declares it goes only to a host whose pkg-config finds it; never provisioned, and a host without it is not drift

xvfb.note: Xvfb, the X server without a display, which a desktop app's end-to-end test runs the real app in: a capability only some Linux hosts have (an admin's system package, xvfb); Xvfb has no version option, so the probe prints a constant only when Xvfb -help runs (exit 0); never provisioned, and a host without it is not drift

clang.note: Pinned Ubuntu Clang 21.1.8 (6ubuntu1), which a repo's C99 golden/IR generation checks require fail-closed: a capability installed on the Linux CI hosts as a system package, probed by exact first-line identity so unpinned builds never satisfy it; never provisioned, and a host without it is not drift

vp.probe: t="$HOME/.local/share/ship-queue-ci"; [ -x "$t/bin/vp" ] && [ "$(command -v vp 2>/dev/null)" = "$t/bin/vp" ] && [ -f "$t/vite-plus/current/bin/.vp-setup-complete" ] && [ -f "$t/vite-plus/current/node_modules/.vp-install-complete" ] && python3 -c "import json, os, sys; t = sys.argv[1]; c = json.load(open(t + '/vite-plus/config.json')); pm = c.get('packageManagerShimModes') or {}; ver = os.path.basename(os.path.realpath(t + '/vite-plus/current')); ok = os.path.basename(os.path.realpath(t + '/vp')) == 'vp-' + ver and c.get('nodeShimMode', 'managed') == 'managed' and pm.get('pnpm') == 'managed' and pm.get('npm') == 'managed'; sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)" "$t" 2>/dev/null && VP_HOME="$t/vite-plus" "$t/bin/vp" --version 2>/dev/null | head -1 | grep .
vp.note: Vite+ CLI (vp): used by marscode for workspace install, lint, format, typecheck, and vitest; ci-vp.sh installs the pinned GitHub release tarball for Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64 or macOS arm64, checked against vp-checksums.txt sha256 per platform, into <data root>/ship-queue-ci/vp-<version>, keeps Vite+'s home on the data root (<data root>/ship-queue-ci/vite-plus, linked from ~/.local/share/ship-queue-ci/vite-plus and exported as VP_HOME by CI_PATH_SETUP so a desktop user's ~/.vite-plus is never read or changed), links only vp, vpr and vpx in ship-queue-ci/bin (never node or pnpm shims, so other repos keep ship-queue-ci's pinned node and pnpm), and runs vp env on so Vite+ manages project toolchains instead of falling back to ship-queue-ci's pnpm 9; the probe checks that vp on PATH resolves to ship-queue-ci/bin/vp, matching setup markers (so a probe never triggers self-setup or writes to disk), and managed mode for node, pnpm and npm in vite-plus/config.json

sccache.note: Shared Rust compilation cache installed via infra/ci-host/ci-sccache.sh

guards.install: rn=$(bash "$CI_HOST_PAYLOAD/infra/ci-host/ci-node.sh" real-node); src="$HOME/Dev"; data="${SHIP_QUEUE_DATA_ROOT:-$src}"; HOST_GUARDS_SOURCE_ROOT="$src" HOST_GUARDS_DATA_ROOT="$data" HOST_GUARDS_SCAN_ROOTS="${HOST_GUARDS_SCAN_ROOTS:-$src:$data}" bash "$CI_HOST_PAYLOAD/packages/host-guards/scripts/install.sh" ${rn:+--real-node "$rn"} "$@"
guards.note: the host guards, from the same a repo copy, with the host's own roots (its HOME/Dev, and its data root); run last, after node is in place
